description: Hand-written synthetic teaching examples for evaluator development. These are not university lecture notes or held-out assessment questions.

materials.title: IP addressing
materials.text:
IP addressing
A subnet mask separates the network portion of an IP address from the host portion.
A default gateway forwards packets destined for networks outside the local subnet.

materials.title: Domain names
materials.text:
Domain name resolution
DNS translates domain names into IP addresses. A DNS cache stores recently resolved records until their time to live expires.
An authoritative DNS server provides records for a domain it is responsible for.

materials.title: Transport protocols
materials.text:
Transport protocols
TCP provides reliable ordered delivery using acknowledgements and retransmission. UDP sends datagrams without guaranteeing delivery or ordering.
A port number identifies an application endpoint on a host.

materials.title: Iteration
materials.text:
Iteration
A for loop iterates over the items of a sequence. A while loop repeats while its condition remains true.
A break statement exits the innermost loop immediately. A continue statement skips to the next iteration.

materials.title: Functions
materials.text:
Functions
A parameter is a name in a function definition; an argument is a value supplied when the function is called.
A return statement ends function execution and sends a result to the caller. A local variable is scoped to its function.

materials.title: Python collections
materials.text:
Python collections
A Python list is a mutable ordered sequence. A tuple is an immutable sequence.
A dictionary maps unique keys to values. A set contains distinct elements and can remove duplicates from an iterable.

materials.title: Relational keys
materials.text:
Relational keys
A primary key uniquely identifies a row and cannot be null. A foreign key references a key in a related table to enforce referential integrity.
A composite key uses two or more columns together to identify a row.

materials.title: Transactions
materials.text:
Transactions
Atomicity means a transaction's changes all succeed or none take effect. Durability means committed changes survive a system failure.
A rollback discards uncommitted changes. Isolation controls how concurrent transactions observe one another's changes.

materials.title: Indexes and normalisation
materials.text:
Indexes and normalisation
An index can accelerate lookups but consumes storage and adds work to inserts, updates, and deletes.
Normalisation reduces duplicated facts and helps avoid insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.
